title: Privileged Secrets Handoff Procedures
content:
Purpose:
This playbook defines operational procedures for handing off privileged secrets and emergency (break-glass) access at Redwood Inference. It focuses on: vaulting conventions, short-term credential issuance, rotation cadence, RBAC v2 role checks during handoffs, audit log schema expectations, and automated evidence export to SIEM.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to all privileged secrets stored in the central vault (HashiCorp Vault and cloud KMS-wrapped secrets) and any temporary credentials issued for emergency access.
- Covers both planned handoffs (maintenance windows, planned escalations) and unplanned break-glass events.
- Not a replacement for incident response runbooks; this document is focused on secrets lifecycle and audit/evidence collection.

Primary owners and contacts:
- Secrets/Key Management Owner: Aisha Patel (security-compliance)
- On-call SRE (escalation for urgent handoffs): SRE Oncall rotation
- Vault Operators: Marcus Chen, Rita Gomez

High-level constraints and policies:
- All privileged handoffs must be recorded in the ticketing system with a unique ticket ID.
- RBAC v2 roles must be validated before granting any temporary access.
- Break-glass credentials must be time-limited (max 8 hours) and rotated automatically after issuance.
- Audit logs must be shipped to the SIEM (Splunk) in near real-time and include the fields in the Audit Log Schema below.

RBAC v2 mapping (quick reference):
- role:secrets-reader: read-only vault paths; used for low-privilege automation.
- role:secrets-writer: allowed to create/rotate non-privileged secrets under app/* paths.
- role:privileged-operator: can request temporary credentials for emergency tasks (requires 2-step approval for planned windows).
- role:vault-admin: full vault policy; only human users with Justified Business Need (JBN) and approved by Security.
- role:breakglass-approver: a designated manager or SecOps engineer who can sign off break-glass issuance.

Planned handoff workflow (maintenance / scheduled privileged access):
1) Create ticket in JIRA with scope, owner, affected systems, start/end times, and rollback plan. Ticket must reference vault paths involved.
2) Attach RBAC audit: list of current principals with access to the affected paths (export RBAC v2 snapshot).
3) Request temporary access using the Secrets Handoff form (link in linked_artifacts). The request must explicitly state required access duration (max 24 hours for planned tasks).
4) Approvals: For any role:privileged-operator request, obtain 2 approvers (team manager + breakglass-approver). Record approvals in the ticket.
5) Vault issuance: Vault operator uses vaulted dynamic credentials where possible (AWS/STSM secrets). If static secrets must be used, generate a new secret path prefixed with ad-hoc/{ticket-id}/ and mark as expiring.
6) Automated evidence collection: enable verbose audit for the ticket window and tag logs with ticket_id. Ensure SIEM export connector is active.
7) Work completes: operator rotates or revokes temporary secrets, updates ticket with verification, and closes ticket after 24h verification.
8) Post-handoff review: collect audit artifacts and drop into the evidence bucket referenced in the ticket.

Break-glass (unplanned emergency) workflow:
- Goal: grant the minimum required access for the shortest period while capturing proof and approvals after the fact when necessary.
- Preconditions: Break-glass may be used when immediate access is required to restore service and normal approval path is unavailable.

Steps:
A) Request: Initiating engineer pages SecOps/SRE Oncall with high-priority tag and provides minimal context and affected system.
B) Justification: Engineer records a short justification in the ticket with "breakglass_reason" and the impacted system. If ticket cannot be created immediately, create one as soon as practical.
C) Temporary credential issuance: Vault operator issues a time‑bound dynamic credential (recommended) or creates an ad-hoc secret path ad-hoc/{ticket-id}/breakglass/. Expiration default 4 hours; not to exceed 8 hours without post-hoc approver sign-off.
D) Immediate evidence capture: The operator enables full vault audit logging for the ticket timeframe and forces SIEM export of the audit stream with a "breakglass:true" tag.
E) Post-hoc approvals: Within 8 hours, the breakglass-approver must confirm the necessity and either approve continuation (rare) or require immediate revocation.
F) Rotation & cleanup: All breakglass secrets must be rotated/revoked within the declared expiry and an incident follow-up must include a secrets inventory delta.

Vaulting best practices for handoffs:
- Use dynamic, short-lived cloud credentials (IAM role assume/STS) wherever possible.
- Never share long-term root-like secrets via chat or email; use vault's one-time secret feature or temporary paths.
- Label all ad-hoc secret paths with ticket-id and owner: metadata: {"ticket_id": "JIRA-...", "requester": "user@example.com", "reason": "maintenance"}. (If metadata cannot be stored directly, include it in the ticket and evidence store.)
- Enable kv-engine versioning for critical paths and keep last 7 versions for rollback.

Rotation policy and automation notes:
- High-privilege static secrets: rotate quarterly or after any suspected compromise.
- Break-glass/temporary credentials: automatic rotation policy enforced at time of issuance. Default TTL 4h, max 8h.
- Automation: use the secrets-rotation lambda (ops/rotations) to schedule rotations and generate rotation evidence. Rotation jobs write an entry to the audit stream with fields described in Audit Log Schema.

Audit Log Schema (required fields for SIEM):
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC timestamp of the event.
- event_id: UUIDv4 unique event id.
- event_type: e.g., secret.read, secret.create, secret.rotate, secret.delete, auth.login, policy.update.
- principal_id: canonical user/service id (e.g., user:alice, svc:github-actions).
- principal_role: RBAC v2 role at time of the event (best-effort snapshot).
- ticket_id: JIRA-xxxx or "none" (must be populated for handoffs).
- secret_path: vault path affected (ad-hoc/{ticket}/...).
- operation_result: success|failure.
- correlation_id: request trace id (if present).
- duration_ms: operation latency.
- request_payload_summary: short hash or truncated payload (never include raw secret material).
- reason: free-form justification string (if provided).

Example audit line (JSON single-line for SIEM ingest):
{"timestamp":"2025-01-18T15:12:03Z","event_id":"3f9b3f10-6c2d-4d2e-9b3b-1a2f3c4d5e6f","event_type":"secret.create","principal_id":"user:marcus.chen","principal_role":"role:privileged-operator","ticket_id":"JIRA-SEC-512","secret_path":"ad-hoc/JIRA-SEC-512/breakglass/db-admin","operation_result":"success","duration_ms":122,"reason":"restore critical DB after failover"}

Evidence automation and SIEM export connectors:
- Connector behavior: The vault audit stream is forwarded to an aggregator (log-collector) which enriches events with identity resolution (map principal_id -> human-readable email), and then forwards to Splunk with index=secrets_audit.
- Ensure that the connector tags events with ticket_id, breakglass flag, and RBAC snapshot.
- Evidence artifacts to collect per handoff: audit log slice (timeboxed), RBAC snapshot, list of secrets changed with old/new version IDs (not secret contents), rotation job run logs, approver emails/acknowledgements.
- Evidence storage: store artifacts in the evidence S3 bucket under evidence/{ticket_id}/ with retention policy 365 days (encrypted).

Post-incident verification checklist (to be completed within 24h):
- [ ] Confirm all temporary credentials revoked or rotated.
- [ ] Validate audit log slice present in SIEM.
- [ ] Attach RBAC snapshot to ticket.
- [ ] Confirm no residual ad-hoc paths remain.
- [ ] Schedule follow-up rotation for any statics touched outside rotation policy.
- [ ] Document lessons learned and update this playbook if gaps found.

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- If SIEM connector downtime prevents immediate export: store a local copy of the audit slice and re-upload once the connector is healthy. Record this in the ticket and reference evidence-s3 path.
- If RBAC v2 snapshot tool fails: manually export policy files and include approver attestations in ticket.
- If operator cannot issue dynamic credentials (cloud outage): escalate to SecOps for out-of-band generation and record additional approvals.

Helpful commands / quick snippets:
- Export RBAC snapshot (internal tool): rbacctl snapshot --roles role:privileged-operator --output /tmp/rbac-snapshot.json
- Issue dynamic AWS creds (vault): vault write aws/creds/redwood-ops lease_ttl=4h role=emergency-operator
- Revoke secret path: vault kv delete -force ad-hoc/JIRA-SEC-512/breakglass/db-admin
- Pull audit slice for ticket: vault-audit-tail --from "2025-01-18T14:00:00Z" --to "2025-01-18T16:00:00Z" --ticket JIRA-SEC-512 > /tmp/evidence-audit.json

Retention and compliance notes:
- Evidence retention follows policy: operational evidence (1 year), longer retention only with legal hold.
- Access to evidence S3 bucket is limited to security-compliance and audit roles.
- Regular audits will sample a subset of handoffs every quarter for completeness and policy compliance.

Appendix A: Minimal SIEM query examples (Splunk)
- Search all breakglass events for ticket: index=secrets_audit ticket_id="JIRA-SEC-512" | table timestamp principal_id event_type secret_path operation_result
- Failed secret operations in last 24h: index=secrets_audit operation_result="failure" | where timestamp>relative_time(now(), "-24h")

Appendix B: FAQ
Q: When is it okay to issue a long-lived secret?
A: Only when dynamic credentials are not available AND a business justification is approved. Long-lived secrets must be rotated immediately after use and logged as high priority.

Q: Who can be a breakglass-approver?
A: A designated SecOps engineer or manager listed in the breakglass approvers roster (maintained in Confluence).

Next steps and open items:
- (Action) Build a small UI in internal console to attach ticket_id automatically to vault audit events (owner: Marcus Chen, due 2025-02-01).
- (Action) Add automatic archival of rotation job logs to evidence S3 (owner: Rita Gomez, due 2025-02-15).
- Review cadence: quarterly review of this playbook and rotation thresholds.

References:
- Vault best practices (internal Confluence) CONFLUENCE-SEC-234
- Secrets rotation automation repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/tree/main/rotations
- SIEM ingest schema (Splunk): CONFLUENCE-SEC-312

End of document.
